newsitem.title: GERMANY: DAG union breaks off talks with Lufthansa.
newsitem.headline: DAG union breaks off talks with Lufthansa.

text.p: German white collar union DAG on Thursday afternoon broke off negotiations with Lufthansa AG in the current round of pay talks for the airline's 50,000 employees, a DAG spokesman said on Thursday.
The leader of DAG's negotiating team Michael Tarp told Reuters that the offer made by the airline on Wednesday night was "all in all not acceptable."

"We would have come out with less than the inflation rate if we had taken up the offer," said Tarp, adding that DAG planned to re-enter talks with the company in around four weeks time and expected a better offer from the company then.
The public sector union OeTV, which is simultaneously in negotiations with Lufthansa, said on Thursday it would continue its discussions on the company's proposals.

"We are continuing talks. We may be able to give an evaluation of our talks with Lufthansa later in the evening," an OeTV spokesman said. Traditionally Lufthansa holds separate talks with DAG and OeTV.

Late on Wednesday evening, Lufthansa made a wage proposal to run over the 27 months to the end of 1998. This includes a 30 percent of base salary one-off payment for the remainder of 1996 and for 1997, followed by a 1.3 percent pay rise in 1998.
The offer also includes 500 marks worth of Lufthansa stock as part of a unique profit-sharing scheme for a German company still partially state-owned.
OeTV had earlier demanded a 2.3 percent wage rise while DAG was looking for a four percent increase in wages for the 50,000 workers covered by the contract.
